chunks: Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from Abū Yaḥyā al-Wāsiṭī, from some of his companions, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I said: May I be your ransom, I wash my face, then I wash my hand, and Shayṭān causes me to doubt that I have not washed my forearm and my hand. He عليه السلام said: “If you find the coolness of the water on your forearm, then do not repeat.”

key_terms.أَغْسِلُ: I wash; refers to performing the washing acts of wudu (ablution).
key_terms.الشَّيْطَانُ: Shayṭān; the source of insinuating doubt in the act of worship.
key_terms.بَرْدَ الْمَاءِ: The coolness of the water; a sensory sign indicating that washing has occurred.
key_terms.ذِرَاعِي: My forearm; the limb about which doubt arises in the narration.
key_terms.فَلَا تُعِدْ: Then do not repeat; the legal instruction not to redo the act.
key_terms.وَجْهِي: My face; the face is one of the obligatory parts washed in wudu (ablution).
key_terms.يُشَكِّكُنِي: He causes me to doubt; refers to Satanic misgivings and uncertainty.

ai.seo_question: What should I do if I doubt during wudu (ablution) whether I washed my arm properly?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses doubt during wudu (ablution), specifically after washing the face and hand. Imam Abu ʿAbdillah عليه السلام instructs that if a person can still feel the coolness of the water on the forearm, they should not repeat the washing, indicating that such misgivings should be disregarded.
